sar.narrative: Suspicious Activity Report for CASE-009 documents a coordinated micro-payment fraud ring involving 10 connected cards (SC-09000-K1 through SC-09009-K2) and a shared device fingerprint across 17 cards [EV-04fdd351, EV-1a8bba2c]. The investigation was initiated when transaction 4012185 ($14.50) received a risk score of 0.48, indicating a coordinated micro-payment ring [EV-9d1f20ca]. Analysis of the primary card SC-03009-K955 revealed anomalous velocity: 4 online transactions within 48 hours against a historical average of $3.00 per transaction [EV-2278aead, EV-c261f6ee]. Device-level linkage exposed a fraud ring of 18 cards with 4 confirmed fraud instances, suggesting organized card-testing activity consistent with prior cases CC-4326, CC-4303, CC-4301, CC-4302, CC-4304 [EV-1a8bba2c, EV-c3dc7ed2]. The customer reported no authorization of the disputed transactions and confirmed physical card possession, supporting unauthorized use [EV-22c564e1]. Total exposure across four affected transactions (4012203, 4012204, 4012185, 4012205) reached $2,102.44 with a fraud probability of 0.808. The pattern is classified as undocumented, though keyword retrieval associates it with card_testing methodologies observed in five prior closed cases [EV-c3dc7ed2]. One prior case for this customer was cleared as legitimate, indicating no persistent customer-level fraud history [EV-91402c82]. The evidence supports a verdict of fraud with recommended card termination and ring-wide monitoring.
